name: Tesseract
baseline: EasyOCR (PyTorch CRAFT+CRNN, run on GPU with batch_size 16)
workload: OCR throughput in pages per second over the standard profile (215 pages: 50 historical book pages, 50 olmOCR-bench document pages, 60 handwriting pages, 55 synthetic stress pages) on five Colab runtime types, Tesseract 5 LSTM (eng+fra+deu+lat, --oem 1 --psm 3, one process per page across all CPU cores, OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1) against EasyOCR and other OCR engines.
claimed_speedup: Pages/s, Tesseract 5 vs EasyOCR: 3.47 vs 1.11 on G4 (AMD EPYC 9B45, 48 vCPU), 0.81 vs 0.49 on A100-40GB, 0.82 vs 0.45 on L4, 0.68 vs 0.34 on T4, 2.28 vs 0.20 on TPU-v6e-1 host CPU; roughly 1.7x to 3.1x on the GPU runtimes and about 11x on the TPU host (ratios derived from page data). Also 3.47 vs 1.35 for Surya 0.17 (classic) and 3.47 vs 3.14 for docTR on G4. Not a win everywhere: PaddleOCR 3 is 4.13 pages/s on G4 and docTR is 1.03 vs 0.81 on A100.
hardware: Google Colab runtimes; G4 run recorded as NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with AMD EPYC 9B45, 48 vCPU, 176.9 GB RAM; L4 run recorded as Intel Xeon CPU @ 2.20GHz, 12 vCPU; T4, A100-40GB and TPU-v6e-1 host CPUs not read
tradeoffs: CPU-only engine, no GPU needed. Much lower accuracy than modern OCR VLMs in the same leaderboard (67.8% mean accuracy vs 94.7% for the top engine; handwriting CER 56.1%, stress-track CER 19.0%). Classic engines read in raster order and interleave columns on multi-column pages. Needs per-language traineddata files; scales by running many single-threaded processes.
caveats: Third-party, single-author harness (kvenanzi/ocr, 0 stars, 48 commits, earliest benchmark runs dated 2026-10-02), not peer reviewed and not a well-known suite. The speed rows compare Tesseract on CPU cores against EasyOCR on the GPU, so it is a cost-of-hardware comparison, not like-for-like. Tesseract install is an apt/pytesseract package; build flags and exact version (README says only 'Tesseract 5') are not stated, so this is not tier A. Standard profile is about 215 pages, and the README notes small samples. Tesseract loses throughput to PaddleOCR 3 (4.13 vs 3.47 pages/s on G4) and PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 (5.84 on G4), and to docTR on A100. The project's own tessdoc Benchmarks.md (https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdoc/blob/main/Benchmarks.md, opened) only compares Tesseract versions and build flags on one image (e.g. tessdata_best: 4.1.3 without AVX 37.6052 s vs with AVX 12.7300 s vs 5.0.1 6.1981 s), and shows 3.05 with the legacy engine faster than 5.0.1 on the plain tessdata model (2.4713 s vs 2.9107 s), so it gives no external-baseline win. Category image-codecs is the closest wave-10 category; OCR is image analysis, not a codec.
found_via: seed-list mining backfill: awesome-cpp 'Image Processing' list entry for tesseract-ocr (https://github.com/fffaraz/awesome-cpp#Image Processing); then WebSearch 'OCR benchmark tesseract vs easyocr vs paddleocr CPU speed seconds per image github', which led to github.com/kvenanzi/ocr (results/LEADERBOARD.md, results/hardware.csv, results/runs/*/env.json, ocrbench/engines/tesseract.py)
